newsitem.title: USA: Dade, Broward Cty, Fla., see property values rise.
newsitem.headline: Dade, Broward Cty, Fla., see property values rise.

text.p: Florida's two largest counties, Dade and Broward, saw significant increases in the value of their property over the past year, appraisers said.
The value of Dade County property rose by 3.8 percent or $2.94 billion to $80.5 billion. New construction accounted for $1.7 billion of the increase, Property Appraiser Herbert Parlato said.
Miami, the Dade County seat, saw a 3.2 percent increase in total property value while Hialeah had a 6.3 percent increase and Miami Beach saw a 4 percent increase.

In Broward County, total property value rose by $3 billion or 5.2 percent to $57.3 billion, also fueled largely by the construction of new homes and businesses, Property Appraiser William Markham said.
Miramar and Pembroke Pines had the most new construction in Broward and saw their total property values rise 18.2 and 14.4 percent, respectively.
Fort Lauderdale, the county's largest city, saw a 5 percent increase in total property value and a 3.8 percent increase in the value of existing property.
